# Venera-Next compatibility integration

`init.js` is the unmodified `assets/init.js` from Venera-Next commit `4ac4a4e68644dc51ecee5144dd9398d071692e25` (upstream version `1.18.0+234`). Its SHA-256, repository, revision and license checksum are recorded in `UPSTREAM.json`. The upstream JavaScript library is distributed under GPL-3.0; the matching license text is preserved in `LICENSE`.

The compatibility baseline is pinned independently from Kaleid’s product version. The app keeps the upstream source-facing API, including `Network` request overloads and `extra`, binary responses, image fallback hooks, and the runtime-owned `source_id` identity on source data calls. Kaleid validates each identity inside the source isolate. The vendored file is not patched to add app-specific behaviour. The host default User-Agent matches the pinned `lib/foundation/consts.dart` `webUA` value (Chrome 119 on Windows); a source-provided value takes precedence.

Kaleid’s integration lives in `src/main/onlineComics/` and `src/renderer/src/OnlineComics.tsx`. It supplies bounded QuickJS execution, Cheerio DOM objects, Electron Session networking, per-source persistent cookies, host storage, login UI, image processing, resource-protocol delivery and durable downloads. Each source has an independent, terminable runtime and Electron Session; late work cannot mutate a replacement instance. QuickJS, encoding, crypto and Sharp are host-side implementations, not copied from Venera-Next.

Electron Session requests use the app’s normal system proxy and operating-system DNS routing. The Venera-Next JavaScript request API preserves source overrides and cache hints, and HTTP responses retain their status/body for source-level handling. `http_client: dart:io` uses the native Node request path on direct routes and shares the source’s Electron Session cookie store; proxy-routed requests stay on that Session transport. Kaleid does not solve Cloudflare or site challenges. A site-declared domain/mirror setting remains available in that source’s settings, and a 403 is reported as access denial or a challenge rather than assumed login failure.

Site scripts are installed separately from the user-configured repository and are not included in app releases. No upstream site script has been modified or bundled. Third-party notices and the compatible source archive are updated with this integration; this is not an official Venera-Next release.

Source initialization waits for HTTP work started by `init()` and follow-up HTTP requests within the existing 180-second operation budget. This includes scripts that launch API discovery without returning its promise, such as CopyManga. The host shares the current comic's successful/in-flight `loadInfo` within a source instance, preserving source-side initialization fields without repeating the detail requests for each chapter. Explicit refreshes, comic switches, and new source instances reload that context.

Detail chapters and thumbnails are independent capabilities, matching the pinned `comic_details/comic_page.dart`. Kaleid keeps its internal null-ID body chapter for existing progress/download identities while hiding that synthetic chapter in details. Static `thumbnails` and cursor-based `comic.loadThumbnails(id, next)` use the thumbnail request hooks, not body loading. Sprite thumbnail references support the upstream `@x=start-end&y=start-end` syntax; source response processing precedes cropping. Preview assets are distinct from covers, and clicking one supplies a one-shot reader entry page without changing chapter identity. The existing Kaleid detail styling is retained.
